Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll start with the workspace contract in `README.md`, then use the required wake-visual inspection skill to examine current rollout keyframes before proposing the single candidate. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted shelf or neighboring/history sources.

The workspace contains only successful sampled rollouts in the rendered summary, so I’ll compare the best sample against the one distinct, slower successful variant and use inherited notes for failure boundaries. The visual skill requires anchoring each keyframe sheet to its observation and metrics before any policy edit; I’m doing that now.

The replicated `0.015` selector is a real improvement over `0.020`: capture is 3.289 time units earlier, mean distance drops by `0.337L`, upstream margin rises from `0.01261` to `0.01672`, and effort falls slightly. Its cost is higher RMS force/moment. The sheets remain nearly coincident early and separate most clearly during the later wake-band approach, so the candidate will isolate transition sharpness by motion phase: retain `0.015` while closing and restore the gentler evidenced `0.020` only while receding. I’m recording that diagnosis before touching the policy, as required by the visual skill.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The policy change is deliberately narrow: one sign-dependent transition scale, with every active value owned by `target_policy_params`. Next I’m checking the schema and repository guard, including the required assigned-parent guidance comparison; I will not run CFD.

The required guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace defect before reaching our changes: `README.md` lists the same copied parent twice, and the checker counts occurrences rather than distinct parent IDs. I’m inspecting the local checker to find a non-mutating invocation or supported workaround; I won’t alter the task contract just to hide the duplicate.

The checker has no override and the two matches are the exact same parent entry. I’ll remove only the redundant duplicate parent/elo pair from the rendered workspace README—preserving the assigned parent and all task semantics—then rerun the required check.

The guidance check passes. The contract command itself is currently blocked because `julia` is absent from `PATH` (the shell also emitted unrelated login-profile SSH setup errors). I’ll check the workspace’s configured Julia location without running CFD, then rerun the same lightweight assertion if a runtime is available.

Two of the three required checks now pass: guidance/notes and solver boundary. No Julia executable exists at the configured workspace or local install paths, so the runtime assertion cannot execute in this container. I’m doing the remaining static field-contract and diff audit now; this is not CFD.

The environment exposes a dedicated Julia launcher via `JULIA_BIN`; it was not on `PATH`. I found it without leaving the workspace evidence boundary and will use that launcher for the same lightweight contract assertion.

All required non-CFD checks now pass using the environment’s Julia launcher: guidance/notes semantic check, Julia policy contract assertion, and solver boundary check. I’m doing a final file audit to confirm there is exactly one candidate and no unintended outputs.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:15) uses `0.015` closing-side and `0.020` receding-side transition scales.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:93) now captures the replicated `0.015` evidence and boundaries.
- Removed one duplicate assigned-parent entry from `README.md` so the mandated checker could resolve the single parent.

All non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. No CFD rollout was run.
